The **55th Annual [Grammy Awards](Grammy_Award "Grammy Award")** were held on February 10, 2013, at the [Staples Center](Staples_Center "Staples Center") in [Los Angeles](Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") honoring the best in music for the recording year beginning October 1, 2011 through September 30, 2012. The show was broadcast on <CBS> at 8 p.m. ET/PT and was hosted for the second time by [LL Cool J](LL_Cool_J "LL Cool J"). The "Pre-Telecast Ceremony" was streamed live from LA's Nokia Theater at the official Grammy website. Nominations were announced on December 5, 2012, on prime-time television as part of "The GRAMMY Nominations Concert Live! – Countdown to Music's Biggest Night", a one-hour special co-hosted by LL Cool J & [Taylor Swift](Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") and broadcast live on CBS from the [Bridgestone Arena](Bridgestone_Arena "Bridgestone Arena") in [Nashville, Tennessee](Nashville%2C_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee").[[2]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-2) [Fun](Fun_(band) "Fun (band)"), [Frank Ocean](Frank_Ocean "Frank Ocean"), [Mumford & Sons](Mumford_%26_Sons "Mumford & Sons"), <Jay-Z>, [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West") and [Dan Auerbach](Dan_Auerbach "Dan Auerbach") received the most nominations with six each.[[3]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-3)[[4]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-4)

<Gotye> and <Kimbra> won the [Record of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") for "[Somebody That I Used to Know](Somebody_That_I_Used_to_Know "Somebody That I Used to Know")", becoming the second Australian and first New Zealand act to win the award. [Mumford & Sons](Mumford_%26_Sons "Mumford & Sons") won the [Album of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") for *[Babel](Babel_(Mumford_%26_Sons_album) "Babel (Mumford & Sons album)")*, and [Fun](Fun_(band) "Fun (band)") won the [Song of the Year](Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year") (with [Jeff Bhasker](Jeff_Bhasker "Jeff Bhasker")) for "[We Are Young](We_Are_Young "We Are Young")" as well as the [Best New Artist](Grammy_Award_for_Best_New_Artist "Grammy Award for Best New Artist").[[5]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-AP-5) [Kelly Clarkson](Kelly_Clarkson "Kelly Clarkson") won the [Best Pop Vocal Album](Best_Pop_Vocal_Album "Best Pop Vocal Album") for *[Stronger](Stronger_(Kelly_Clarkson_album) "Stronger (Kelly Clarkson album)")*, becoming the first and only artist to win the award twice.[[5]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-AP-5) Dan Auerbach won the most awards during the ceremony, with five (including three as part of [The Black Keys](The_Black_Keys "The Black Keys")); followed by The Black Keys, Gotye, <Jay-Z>, <Skrillex>, [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West"), with three each.[[5]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-AP-5) Other multiple winners include: [Chick Corea](Chick_Corea "Chick Corea"), Fun, Kimbra, Mumford & Sons, [Frank Ocean](Frank_Ocean "Frank Ocean"), [Matt Redman](Matt_Redman "Matt Redman") and [Esperanza Spalding](Esperanza_Spalding "Esperanza Spalding") with two awards each.[[5]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-AP-5)[[6]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-6)[[7]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-7)

The Recording Academy introduced three new categories to the 78 awards previously presented at the [54th ceremony](2012_Grammy_Awards "2012 Grammy Awards")—[Best Classical Compendium](Best_Classical_Compendium "Best Classical Compendium"), [Best Latin Jazz Album](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Latin_Jazz_Album "Grammy Award for Best Latin Jazz Album"), and [Best Urban Contemporary Album](Best_Urban_Contemporary_Album "Best Urban Contemporary Album"), bringing it to a total of 81 awards.[[8]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-8) 70 of them were presented at the pre-telecast at the [Nokia Theatre](Nokia_Theatre_L.A._Live "Nokia Theatre L.A. Live"), with the remaining 11 were presented at the main ceremony.[[9]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-Pre-telecast-9) [Bruce Springsteen](Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen") received the [MusiCares Person of the Year](MusiCares_Person_of_the_Year "MusiCares Person of the Year") award on February 8, 2013, at the 23rd Grammy Benefit Gala at the [Los Angeles Convention Center](Los_Angeles_Convention_Center "Los Angeles Convention Center"), two nights prior to the main ceremony.[[10]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-MusiCares-10) The official poster was designed by Artist Erika Iris Simmons.[[11]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-11) The program producer is AEG Ehrlich Ventures, with Ken Ehrlich serving as executive producer, Louis J. Horvitz as director and David Wild and Ken Ehrlich as writers.[[12]](55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards#cite_note-JT-12)

The **Grammy Award for Best Rap Album** is an award presented to recording artists for quality albums with [rapping](Rapping "Rapping") at the [Grammy Awards](Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), a ceremony that was established in 1958 and originally called the Gramophone Awards.[[1]](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Album#cite_note-Grammy-1) Honors in several categories are presented at the ceremony annually by the [National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences](National_Academy_of_Recording_Arts_and_Sciences "National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences") of the United States to "honor artistic achievement, technical proficiency and overall excellence in the recording industry, without regard to album sales or chart position".[[2]](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Album#cite_note-Overview-2)

In 1995, the Academy announced the addition of the award category Best Rap Album.[[3]](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Album#cite_note-3) The first award was presented to the group [Naughty by Nature](Naughty_by_Nature "Naughty by Nature") at the [38th Grammy Awards](38th_Grammy_Awards "38th Grammy Awards") the following year. According to the category description guide for the [52nd Grammy Awards](52nd_Grammy_Awards "52nd Grammy Awards"), the award is presented for "albums containing at least 51% playing time of tracks with newly recorded rapped performances".[[4]](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Album#cite_note-52nd-4) Award recipients often include the [producers](Record_producer "Record producer"), [engineers](Audio_engineering "Audio engineering"), and/or [mixers](Audio_mixing_(recorded_music) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") associated with the nominated work in addition to the recording artists.[[5]](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Album#cite_note-5)

As of 2023, <Eminem> holds the record for the most wins in this category, with six. [Lauryn Hill](Lauryn_Hill "Lauryn Hill") was the first female artist to win in this category, when she won in 1997 with the <Fugees>. [Cardi B](Cardi_B "Cardi B") became the first solo female rapper to win for *[Invasion of Privacy](Invasion_of_Privacy_(album) "Invasion of Privacy (album)")*.[[6]](Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Album#cite_note-6) [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West") was presented the award four times, [Kendrick Lamar](Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") has received the award three times, and the duo known as <Outkast> and [Tyler, The Creator](Tyler%2C_the_Creator "Tyler, the Creator") have all received the award twice. <Jay-Z> holds the record for the most nominations, with eleven. [Drake](Drake_(rapper) "Drake (rapper)") became the first non-American winner in this category when he won in 2013. [The Roots](The_Roots "The Roots") have received the most nominations without a win, with five. Eminem and West are the only artists to win the award in consecutive years, with Eminem achieving the feat twice. In 2016, Drake's *[If You're Reading This It's Too Late](If_You're_Reading_This_It's_Too_Late "If You're Reading This It's Too Late")* became the first mixtape to get nominated for the award, and in 2017, [Chance the Rapper](Chance_the_Rapper "Chance the Rapper")'s *[Coloring Book](Coloring_Book_(mixtape) "Coloring Book (mixtape)")* became the first mixtape to win the award. In 2019, [Cardi B](Cardi_B "Cardi B") was the first female solo artist to win Best Rap Album.
